title: Smoke Test — Payment Reversal (Manage-Order)
subtitle: Phase B: reverse a recorded offline ledger entry. The original row is never deleted — a linked, negative-amount row of the same type books the correction, restoring the balance. No refund is issued.

meta.Flow: login → event 10 orders → open O-DBIEECO → Payments panel → record $1.57 Cash → reverse it with a required reason → balance restored
meta.Order: O-DBIEECO (id 12), staged to AWAITING_OFFLINE_PAYMENT / $1.57, no Stripe payment
meta.Data: Order 12 staged then restored to COMPLETED/PAYMENT_RECEIVED; test ledger rows 14/15 deleted

steps.title: Payments panel — outstanding balance, empty ledger
steps.description: Owed $1.57 / Collected $0.00 / Outstanding $1.57. Note the low-emphasis 'Comp remaining $1.57' control now carries a thin dashed border + gift icon so it reads as clickable at rest.

steps.title: Record a $1.57 Cash payment
steps.description: Amount defaults to the outstanding balance; method Cash, reference 'receipt #DEV-12'. This creates a positive ledger credit.

steps.title: Order settled — ledger row with reverse affordance
steps.description: Balance reconciles to SETTLED (Collected $1.57). The new Cash row shows the reference and a per-row reverse icon (hover tooltip: 'Reverse this payment').

steps.title: Reverse modal — reason required
steps.description: Explains it books a correcting entry of -$1.57 against the Cash payment, keeps the original for audit, and does NOT issue a refund (offline cash is returned in person). Reason is required.

steps.title: Reason entered
steps.description: 'Wrong amount entered — cash was never collected, correcting the ledger.' The reason becomes the reversal row's audit note.

steps.title: Reversed — balance restored, audit trail intact
steps.description: Ledger now shows a 'Reversal -$1.57' row (red, with the reason) and the original 'Cash' row struck-through with a 'Reversed' badge and no further reverse action. Balance returns to Outstanding $1.57. DB: row 15 reverses_payment_id=14.
